description: Finds new errors in your logs without a model. An agent looks for the cause, and you decide if an agent fixes it.

inputs.name: logs
inputs.label: Logs command
inputs.description: A command that prints recent log lines, for example `tail -n 500 log/app.log`, `docker compose logs --since 1h app` or `journalctl -u app --since "1 hour ago"`.

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.label: Error pattern
inputs.description: Lines that match this regular expression count as errors. Case does not matter.

inputs.name: check
inputs.label: Check
inputs.description: The command that proves a fix, for example `npm test`, `pytest` or `go test ./...`.

outputs.name: finding
outputs.description: The summary, cause, fix and severity of the new errors.

nodes.label: Read the logs
nodes.command:
# No model in this step. It keeps the lines that match, as fingerprints
# without numbers, ids and times, and drops the fingerprints seen before.
set -eu
seen="${NS_KNOWLEDGE:-}/watch-logs/seen.txt"
[ -f "$seen" ] || seen=/dev/null
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
if ! sh -c "{{logs}}" > "$tmp/log" 2>&1; then
	echo "The logs command failed:"
	tail -n 20 "$tmp/log"
	exit 1
fi
export LC_ALL=C
tr '\t' ' ' < "$tmp/log" | tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037\177' \
	| { grep -Ei -e "{{pattern}}" || true; } > "$tmp/hits"
sed -E -e 's/[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F-]{27}/<id>/g' \
	-e 's/0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9a-fA-F]{16,}/<id>/g' \
	-e 's/[0-9]+/<n>/g' -e 's/ +/ /g' -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
	"$tmp/hits" > "$tmp/prints"
# One example line per new fingerprint, at most 50.
paste "$tmp/prints" "$tmp/hits" \
	| awk -F '\t' 'FILENAME == ARGV[1] { seen[$0] = 1; next } !($1 in seen) && !($1 in shown) { shown[$1] = 1; print }' "$seen" - \
	| head -n 50 > "$tmp/new"
if [ ! -s "$tmp/new" ]; then
	echo "No new errors."
	exit 0
fi
# The lines on stdin as one JSON string.
json() {
	sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g' \
		| awk 'BEGIN { printf "\"" } { printf "%s%s", (NR > 1 ? "\\n" : ""), $0 } END { print "\"" }'
}
count=$(wc -l < "$tmp/new" | tr -d ' ')
echo "$count new kinds of error."
printf '{"outcome":"new","count":%s,"lines":%s,"fingerprints":%s}\n' "$count" \
	"$(cut -f 2- "$tmp/new" | json)" "$(cut -f 1 "$tmp/new" | json)" > "$NS_OUTPUT"

nodes.label: Find the cause
nodes.prompt:
These lines are new in the logs of this project, one line per kind of error:

```
{{read.data.lines}}
```

Find their cause in the code of your working directory. Read the code and its git history. Do not change any file.

Report one outcome:
- `found`: a real problem. Propose the smallest fix.
- `noise`: expected or harmless. Say why in `cause`.
- `fail`: you cannot find the cause. Say what you checked in `cause`.

Always fill in `summary` (one sentence: what goes wrong), `cause`, `fix` ("None." when nothing needs a fix) and `severity`.

outcomes.name: found
outcomes.description: The errors point to a real problem.

outcomes.name: noise
outcomes.description: The errors are expected or harmless.

nodes.message: No agent found the cause of the new errors.

nodes.label: Fix or ignore?

options.name: fix
options.description: An agent makes the fix and runs your check. It reads your note.

options.name: ignore
options.description: Night Shift does not show these errors again.

nodes.message: The fix did not pass your check. The next run looks at these errors again.

nodes.label: Remember these errors
nodes.command:
# Adds the fingerprints to the list that later runs skip.
set -eu
if [ -z "${NS_KNOWLEDGE:-}" ]; then
	echo "This step needs the project's knowledge folder."
	exit 1
fi
seen="$NS_KNOWLEDGE/watch-logs/seen.txt"
mkdir -p "$NS_KNOWLEDGE/watch-logs"
if [ ! -f "$seen" ]; then
	echo "# Log errors that watch-logs does not show again, one per line." > "$seen"
fi
printf '%s\n' "{{read.data.fingerprints}}" >> "$seen"
echo "Added {{read.data.count}} kinds of error to watch-logs/seen.txt."
